LESSON: INDIGENOUS KENYAN CRAFTS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.11: Indigenous Kenyan Crafts
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Indigenous Kenyan Crafts, part of Creating and Performing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 9 CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS.

Key inquiry question: Why is clay the preferred material for pottery? 2. How is a fabric woven?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe coil techniques in pottery,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indigenous Kenyan Crafts in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. model a vessel using coil method,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indigenous Kenyan Crafts in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Indigenous Kenyan Crafts together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: learner makes a fabric using 2/1 twill weaving technique,

• Communication and collaboration: learner collaboratively fires the bone dry vessel using an open pit kiln.

• Self-efficacy: learner displays and talk about own and peers’ articles.

47

Values:
● Respect: the learner gains respect for others’ opinions while creating and sharing on own and peers’ articles.

● Responsibility: the learner acquires self-discipline as when making a wooden mitre joint frame loom.

● Patriotism: the learner gains appreciation for Indigenous Kenyan Crafts through pottery items from actual and virtual

sources and coil technique periods.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Hygiene and safety: the learner fire the bone dry vessel using an open pit kiln.

• Environmental conservation: the learner sources clay and prepares clay.

Link to other Learning areas

Agriculture and nutrition: learner sources clay thus understanding types of soils.

The learner MUST cover at least ONE of these areas:
